exposure: maternal demographic characteristics (age, gravidity, antenatal visits, booking status)
maternal conditions (pre-eclampsia, diabetes, hypertensive diseases, gestational diabetes)
fetal causes (prematurity, non-viable congenital abnormalities, selective growth restriction)
cohort: The study included all cases of intrauterine fetal death admitted to the department of obstetrics and gynecology at a tertiary care centre in Srikakulam, India, during a one-year period.
finding: Maternal conditions, particularly hypertensive diseases (75%) and gestational diabetes (18.75%), were the most common contributors to intrauterine deaths (58.18%), with 87.27% occurring antepartum, while fetal causes accounted for 25.45% of cases.
